9978a77a49.q: What is the correlation between global crude oil prices above $100 per barrel and corn prices at $6 or higher?
9978a77a49.a: Going back to the beginning of 2000, there were roughly 54 months where global crude was above 100 dollars a barrel. Of those 54 months, there was only 12 where global corn wasn't at least $6. When you have $100 crude, you have $6 corn—that's how the math has worked out historically.

f: In his 24-year career, Steve Brewer has experienced an unprecedented shift in mortgage interest rates. Three weeks before this conversation, interest rates on mortgages reached levels higher than at any point in his entire career. This represents a fundamental reversal from the conditions that defined his professional success. Throughout his two decades in the business, the cost of capital had consistently gotten cheaper every year, creating favorable conditions for farmland investments and making it relatively easy to achieve strong returns.

This dramatic change in interest rate environment marks a significant turning point for Brewer and the agricultural finance sector. For the first time in his 24-year tenure, he is confronting a scenario where capital is becoming more expensive rather than cheaper. He acknowledges that much of his success and that of People's Company has been built on this long period of declining capital costs, but now faces a completely different economic landscape that requires rethinking traditional approaches to farmland investment and valuation.
